transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-11 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Torres (CSM); Dr. Priya Rao, Jordan Lee, Taylor Ng (Meditech Health)
Recording link: https://redwood.example.com/recordings/ff-2026-08-11-8421

---

[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I'm Alex Morgan from Redwood — I'll run a quick agenda: SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning, RBAC mapping, and then quick notes on logs and encryption. Samir's going to jump into the technical config.

[00:18] Dr. Priya Rao: Thanks Alex. We're primarily concerned with least-privilege access and being able to provision/deprovision users quickly. We use Azure AD as our IdP and Okta for some vendor teams so we need flexible SAML + SCIM.

[00:35] Samir (SE): Cool. High level — Redwood supports standard SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM 2.0 for provisioning. For SAML we can operate as a service provider, we provide SP metadata, and you configure Azure AD as the IdP. For SCIM we support group based sync and can map SCIM groups to RBAC roles.

[00:50] Jordan: Quick question — can we sync groups from Azure AD so that when a user is added to "redwood-prod-admins" they get the admin role in Redwood?

[01:05] Samir: Yes — that's the typical pattern. You create a SCIM group in Azure AD and map it to a Redwood role. We recommend two things: keep admin groups small, and use separate groups for sensitive roles. There is an example mapping in the provisioning guide.

[01:22] Taylor: Are there constraints on attribute mapping? We want email + employeeNumber to be authoritative.

[01:35] Samir: We expect immutable unique identifier — email is common. We also support externalId/employeeNumber for de-dupe. Mapping is configurable; I'll send sample attribute mappings in the follow-up.

[01:50] Dr. Priya Rao: How fast is deprovisioning? If someone is removed from the SCIM group, how quickly is access revoked? That's non-negotiable for us.

[02:05] Samir: SCIM events are near real-time, typically within a minute or two. For sessions already issued, we invalidate tokens on the next auth check — session length depends on your org policy; we can shorten session TTLs for stricter orgs.

[02:25] Jordan: Are there service accounts or API keys? How do they fit into RBAC?

[02:35] Alex: Good point — Redwood supports machine/service accounts with scoped API keys and you can assign them to a role with least privilege. Keys are visible to owners only and can be rotated. For dedicated/private deployments there's an option for hardware-backed keys.

[02:50] Taylor: Speaking of private, we may have to run in a VPC or on-prem for certain patient data. How does SSO work in Private mode?

[03:05] Samir: In Private/VPC mode we offer a customer-managed control plane; SAML still works — you'd configure your IdP to talk to the customer control plane endpoint. For on-prem we have installation docs; sometimes we need a short tunnel to exchange metadata if the endpoint isn't publicly reachable.

[03:25] Dr. Priya Rao: Audit logging — can we stream logs to our Splunk? We need immutable audit trails for privileged operations and user provisioning events.

[03:40] Samir: Yes, we support log export to S3 and direct streaming to common SIEMs via syslog/forwarders. Audit logs include admin activity, SCIM provisioning events, SAML sign-ins, API key creation, model access events — timestamps and actor IDs included. We also provide an event webhook for real-time events.

[03:58] Jordan: Are logs signed or tamper-evident? We have a compliance requirement to retain tamper-evident logs for 1 year.

[04:12] Alex: Our hosted offering provides append-only logs with retention controls and log integrity checks; we can also integrate with your customer-managed S3 with encryption and object lock if you need immutability. We'll include those details in the docs.

[04:30] Taylor: Encryption — we want BYOK (bring your own key) for at-rest encryption. Is that supported?

[04:40] Samir: Yes. For hosted we integrate with major cloud KMS providers — AWS KMS, Google KMS, Azure Key Vault — and we support CMKs. For Dedicated/Private we can support HSM/KMS integrations and provide options for customer-managed keys. Key rotation is supported; we have a documented workflow.

[04:58] Dr. Priya Rao: Any FIPS or HSM details you can share now?

[05:06] Samir: We have FIPS-validated cipher suites at rest and in transit. For HSMs we can do an HSM-backed KMS integration in Dedicated setups; that'll require a short architecture review.

[05:20] Jordan: Regarding compliance artifacts — can you share SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certs? We also need your penetration test cadence.

[05:32] Alex: Absolutely — I'll send SOC2 Type II, ISO summary, and our pentest schedule + summary. We do third-party pen tests annually and internal red-team exercises.

[05:45] Taylor: How about RBAC granularity — can we create custom roles and limit model access? We want devs to have inference-only access to test models but not egress logs or billing.

[06:00] Samir: Yes — role model is flexible. We have predefined roles and you can create custom roles scoped to actions (e.g., generate:text, embeddings:create, view:billing, manage:keys). You can also restrict route-level access. We'll share the RBAC matrix in the follow-up.

[06:18] Jordan: Any gotchas around token expiration or refresh for service accounts?

[06:28] Samir: Service keys are long lived by default but can be configured with TTL and require rotation. OAuth flows for user sessions respect your IdP policies for refresh.

[06:40] Dr. Priya Rao: Data residency — our PHI data for some environments must stay in eu-west-1. Does Redwood provide region pinning?

[06:55] Alex: Yes — you can pin region and specify data residency. For hosted accounts we offer region choices; for Dedicated/Private we'll provision capacity in your requested region. We'll capture your region requirement in the next steps.

[07:10] Taylor: A bit of a squeak — do you persist prompts or model contexts? For our compliance we only want minimal logging and avoid storing prompts with PHI.

[07:23] Samir: We provide controls: session and prompt retention policies, opt-out for prompt logging at a project level, and can redact sensitive fields via tokenization pre-ingest. That said some telemetry is necessary for billing and SLOs — we can minimize stored context and show you the retention settings.

[07:42] Jordan: On SCIM — do you support just-in-time provisioning or full provisioning?

[07:50] Samir: Both. You can do JIT via SAML assertion and also SCIM for full lifecycle provisioning (create, update, delete). SCIM supports group membership sync.

[08:02] Alex: Okay let's talk about a test plan — we recommend: 1) exchange SP/IdP metadata, 2) deploy SCIM connector in your Azure AD to a staging account, 3) validate group to role mappings with 6 test users, 4) test deprovisioning and log export to your Splunk/S3.

[08:20] Dr. Priya Rao: Sounds good. One more question — can you provide attestations for encryption standards and key management?

[08:28] Alex: Yes, those are in the security whitepaper I'll share. It'll include cipher suites, key rotation frequency, KMS integration patterns, and how we handle customer-managed keys.

[08:40] Taylor: Any limitations with SCIM group sizes or rate limits? We manage big groups with 5,000+ users.

[08:50] Samir: SCIM rate limits exist to protect the service — default throttle is modest, but for enterprise we can request quota increases and support bulk imports for onboarding. We'll capture group size in the follow-up.

[09:05] Jordan: For SIEM forwarding, do you support encrypted forwarders and mutual TLS?

[09:12] Samir: Yes we support mTLS for log endpoints and secure forwarding. If you want direct Splunk HTTP Event Collector integration we can show config.

[09:22] Dr. Priya Rao: Are there any known gotchas when integrating with Azure AD specifically?

[09:30] Samir: A couple: make sure group-based provisioning is enabled in the AAD app configuration, configure the attribute mapping for userPrincipalName vs. mail depending on your setup, and register correct reply URLs. We'll provide an Azure-specific checklist.

[09:50] Taylor: One operational question — if we want to scope a single team to a Dedicated instance for compliance tests, how fast can you provision?

[09:58] Alex: Typical Dedicated provisioning is weeks (depending on capacity), but for pilot environments we can sometimes spin a constrained environment in a few days. We'll coordinate with infra and put expectations in the follow-up.

[10:12] Jordan: Ok, that's helpful. Can you also include the retention period for audit logs and how to request extended retention?

[10:20] Alex: Yes — default is 90 days for interactive logs, 1 year for audit trails in enterprise packages; extended retention is available as an add-on. We'll include pricing notes in the doc share.

[10:35] Taylor: Anything else on compliance — do you provide evidence for encryption-in-transit?

[10:42] Samir: We use TLS 1.2+ and support TLS 1.3; cert details and cipher suite lists are in the whitepaper.

[10:50] Dr. Priya Rao: Great — I think that covers our concerns. Let's recap next steps.

[11:00] Alex: Recap: Alex to share SOC2/ISO and security whitepaper; Samir to share SAML SP metadata, SCIM guide, RBAC matrix; Jordan to provide test tenant and users; Lina to schedule SSO validation session. We'll target follow-up the week of Aug 17.

[11:20] Jordan: That works. Also, can you enable a read-only role for our auditors to view audit trails?

[11:30] Samir: Yes, we can create an "auditor" read-only role scoped to logs and exports. We'll include the role example.

[11:40] Taylor: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the docs.

[11:45] Alex: Thanks — we'll follow up shortly.
